newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar looks solid at close, TWI above 68.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar looks solid at close, TWI above 68.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer on Thursday after tracking lower overnight in line with a weaker Australian dollar, and dealers said it looked well supported.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.7070/77 and 68.07 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7064/71 and 68.06 at the opening.
Overnight it had dipped as low as 0.7055 in sympathy with the Aussie, which tumbled a cent on gold price weakness and rumours of an official interest rate cut.

"On balance there's still good buying interest around in the Kiwi, and if we were to see the Aussie recover then there's no doubt we'd see further gains for the Kiwi, back up towards that US$0.71 area," a chief dealer said.
He said some further Australian dollar weakness was on the cards, to which Kiwi would not be immune. However, it should continue to perform well on the TWI and against the Aussie.
The U.S. dollar looked well placed for further gains, especially in light of fears over President Boris Yeltsin's health following his readmission to hospital with early signs of pneumonia.
The New Zealand dollar traded a US$0.7059-77 range in a slow session, and a dealer said there was good support around 0.7050.
